newsitem.title: USA: Lower U.S. cattle prices seen in Q1/97.
newsitem.headline: Lower U.S. cattle prices seen in Q1/97.

text.p: A series of cattle auctions in the first quarter of the year could drive cattle prices to as low as $60-$62.00 per cwt, an American Farm Bureau Federation (AFBF) analyst said.
"During the first quarter of 1997 fed cattle supplies could bunch-up, pressuring prices," David Miller, an AFBF livestock specialist, told the AFBF annual convention.
Fed cattle traded at $66.00 in Texas and Kansas last week, industry sources said.
Miller said the bunching of cattle would occur when the large number of cattle placed in feed lots in late 1996 reached market weight in early 1997.
Cattle prices should recover in the second quarter to average $63.00 to $65.00, but fall in the third quarter to average $61.00 to $63.00.
Fourth quarter prices could average from $64.00 to $67.00 and possibly peak at around $70.
